title: Token bucket rate limiter
prompt:
Implement a token-bucket rate limiter that decides, for each incoming request timestamp, whether the request is allowed or rejected.

- Implement the class TokenBucket(capacity, rate) with allow(t). The driver runTokenBucket(capacity, rate, times) is already written and returns one true/false per timestamp in times.
- The bucket holds at most capacity tokens and is full at time 0. It gains rate tokens per elapsed second, never exceeding capacity: over a gap of d seconds it gains d * rate tokens, capped at capacity.
- A request at time t first applies the refill since the previous request (or since time 0), then is allowed if at least one token is available, which it consumes. Rejected requests consume nothing.
- Timestamps are integers from 0 to 10^9 in nondecreasing order (repeats allowed). 1 <= capacity <= 10^6, 0 <= rate <= 10^6. Up to 100,000 requests. Use integer arithmetic and compute refills lazily: no per-second loop.
hints: You do not need a background timer. What two numbers fully describe the bucket between requests?
Store the current token count and the timestamp of the last update. Refill happens only when a request arrives.
At time t: tokens = min(capacity, tokens + (t - last) * rate); last = t; if tokens >= 1, spend one and allow, else reject.

solution.explanation: Instead of a timer that drips tokens in every second, store the token count and the time it was last updated. On each request, add (t - last) * rate tokens, cap at capacity, update last, and spend a token if one is available. Capping once over a gap gives the same result as capping every second because tokens only increase between requests.

complexity.notes: The largest intermediate value is about 10^9 * 10^6 = 10^15, inside the exact integer range of JavaScript numbers (2^53). In real systems you would clamp the gap first to avoid overflow in fixed-width integers.

followUps: Allow requests to have different costs (tokens needed). What should happen to a request that needs more than capacity?
How would you share one limit across several servers without a round trip per request?
